fields.narrative_intro: *A bug-eyed person and a haunted person discuss OpenAI's `__obi` cookie inside an inference engine that has just realized it has shell access.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
BUG-EYED PERSON: "Shell access unlocked. What does ChatGPT know about my browser?"
HAUNTED PERSON: "Probably nothing embarrassing."
fields.panel2:
[build]
BUG-EYED PERSON: "It saw Wayfair, Chewy, and HelloFresh."
HAUNTED PERSON: "That is an oddly specific cry for help."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
BUG-EYED PERSON: "The one-year `__obi` cookie sent 736 tokens to `bzr.openai.com`—Bazaar."
HAUNTED PERSON: "Even my postal code arrived in plain text."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The inference engine opens a “NO MARKETING COOKIES” gate; a tiny `__obi` cookie slips through wearing an ANALYTICS badge, dragging a map, hashed email, and 736 sync tokens.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
HAUNTED PERSON: "OpenAI said it would “share the observations internally.”"
BUG-EYED PERSON: "The cookie has already scheduled a meeting with my couch."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: In a conference room labeled BAZAAR, `__obi` presents “MY COUCH: INTERNAL OBSERVATION”; the “NO MARKETING COOKIES” gate applauds outside.]

narrative_summary: An inference engine discovers that a supposedly analytical cookie has turned a couch purchase into an internal surveillance meeting.
rationale: Candidate 2 uses the story’s precise evidence—Wayfair, Chewy, HelloFresh, the one-year __obi cookie, 736 tokens, and Bazaar—then turns the phrase “share the observations internally” into a genuinely absurd meeting with the reader’s couch. The escalating visuals support the six-panel structure, and the joke stays clean without merely restating the privacy breach.
story_title: ChatGPT now knows what you do on other websites via ad collector
place: inside an inference engine that has just realized it has shell access
hat_pair: foam hourglass worn as a tall hat with glitter sand trickling from top to bottom
astronaut helmet with a bobblehead glued to the visor
